consentTitle: Taking part in a bathroom-planning study
consentIntro: Please read this before you start. Taking part is voluntary and you can stop at any time.
consentText:
[PLACEHOLDER — replace this whole text with the wording approved by your ethics board or IRB, and change consentVersion so every session records which text was shown.]

What you will do: use a bathroom-planning tool to complete a few short design tasks, then answer a short questionnaire about your experience.

What is recorded: which controls you use and when, the designs you create, how long each task takes, and your questionnaire answers. If you upload a photo, only a text description of it is kept unless the study team has told you otherwise. You are given a random participant code. Your name and contact details are not asked for.

Your rights: you can stop at any time by closing the page. You can ask for your data to be deleted at any point using the “Delete my study data” link at the foot of every page.

Who to contact: [study contact details].
consentAgreeLabel: I have read this and I agree to take part.
completionNote: You can now close this page.

tasks.title: A compact family bathroom
tasks.brief: A family of four shares this small bathroom. Fit a toilet, a shower, a vanity and a mirror, with a towel rail. A storage unit would be welcome too, but it may not fit alongside the vanity, or inside the budget. Decide what matters most.

tasks.title: A master bathroom with a bath
tasks.brief: Design a generous master bathroom with a bathtub and a separate shower. Choose the look you prefer, and keep the plan comfortable to walk through.

tasks.title: A tight budget
tasks.brief: The budget is tight. Get the four essentials in, then see how the total responds when you change the look or the fixtures.

questionnaire.title: How was that?
questionnaire.intro: Please rate how much you agree with each statement about the tool you just used, from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree).

items.text: I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
I found the system unnecessarily complex.
I thought the system was easy to use.
I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system.
I found the various functions in this system were well integrated.
I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system.
I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
I found the system very cumbersome to use.
I felt very confident using the system.
I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system.
